newsitem.title: USA: Galoob sees 1996 profits double, sales up sharply.
newsitem.headline: Galoob sees 1996 profits double, sales up sharply.

text.p: Galoob Toys Inc. said Wednesday it expectws annual profits to double and it predicted sharply higher 1996 toy sales despite a shorter holiday shopping season.
The company said it is confident its sales momentum will continue, making 1997 another year of record sales.
Galoob, which makes the popular Sky Dancer ballerina doll, forecast 1996 sales of $280 million to $290 million, up 27 percent to 32 percent from $220 million last year.
Full-year earnings per share will range from $1.20 to $1.25, excluding a first quarter one-time, non-cash charge of $24.3 million from its stock exchange offer, it said.
Galoob said even the low end of the expected earnings range was double last year's profits of $6.3 million, or 60 cents a share.
Net earnings for the fourth quarter will be $13.1 million to $13.7 million, the toy company based in South San Francisco, Calif., said.

Galoob also said its U.S. retail sales have been 34 percent ahead of last year since Thanksgiving. But because there are five fewer shopping days between Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day in 1996 than in 1995, some retailers have been more cautious than usual about placing re-orders late in the season, Galoob said.
Galoob's stock fell 25 cents to $17.25 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
